Restated as 'few slots touched', `pslot` measured 0.4 to 1.2 KB with about 16 groups and creates in 1.6 to 1.8 ms, but its cold open is reasoned, E-36 priced one slot map shared by the project, and a drop out of a shared group was never run (K-06).
MIN-P.closes: phase 1 fixes the formats (run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state); phase 3 or 4: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second, with the cold-open and drop pins

COMP.why: 1.3 line 'SC-13's small, pslot too': as worded, per-slot state costs about 85 B a touched slot, so an idle resource that touched 100 slots is over 2 KB in shared groups too (E-36). Restated as 'few slots touched', `pslot` measured 0.4 to 1.2 KB with about 16 groups and creates in 1.6 to 1.8 ms, but its cold open is reasoned, E-36 priced one slot map shared by the project, and a drop out of a shared group was never run (K-06).
COMP.closes: phase 1 fixes the formats (run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state); phase 3 or 4: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second, with the cold-open and drop pins

SLOG.why: 1.3 line 'SC-13's small': it is a slot row, so per-slot state at about 85 B a touched slot puts an idle resource with 100 touched slots over 2 KB as worded (E-36). Restated it is open: its shape is reasoned to be MIN's (one group a resource, dormant when idle), and a loglet's idle cost was never measured.
SLOG.closes: phase 1 fixes the formats (run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state); phase 3 or 4: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second, with the cold-open and drop pins

OBJ.why: 1.3 line 'SC-13's small': it is a slot row, so per-slot state at about 85 B a touched slot puts an idle resource with 100 touched slots over 2 KB as worded (E-36). Restated it is open: it holds no group in memory (E-26), but its create is a PUT or more and nothing timed create, cold open or drop on a store.
OBJ.closes: phase 1 fixes the formats (run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state); phase 3 or 4: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second, with the cold-open and drop pins

CELL.why: Not a slot row. 16 dormant groups a resource come to about 1.1 KB (16 x 57 B plus the catalog row, reasoned from E-26). But creating 16 groups and waking them cold were not timed against 10.7 ms and 5 ms; E-26 woke 20 groups in 10 to 16 ms.
CELL.closes: E-36's create, cold-open and drop runs for 16 groups a resource

LANE.why: An idle resource costs 0.2 KB with 64 groups a project and creates in 1.6 to 1.8 ms (E-36). Dropping a resource whose records share a lane's log with others, and refusing old cursors of a re-created name, were not modelled or run.
LANE.closes: a model and a run of dropping and re-creating a resource inside shared lanes

SPLIT.why: Not a slot row: one group a resource, dormant when idle (A-15, reasoned), with no slot table and no per-slot state. Nothing measured its idle cost, create, cold open or drop.
SPLIT.closes: E-36's runs for a group per resource with lineage in place of slots

PD.why: TiKV merges the regions of small tables (cross-table merge, cited in SC-13's own source). The cost of an idle table and the create and open times were not measured here.
PD.closes: E-36's runs on a PD-shaped prototype; not planned

ISR.why: Not priced (A-15 says so): every resource has N partition groups, each with its own log file (E-12), and idle fetches meet the frame bar only below about 10,000 partitions (E-25).
ISR.closes: E-36's runs for N partitions a resource

V4.why: Step 1: in v4 each resource is its own cluster, with its own port, membership and heartbeats (DESIGN-V5 4.1). Step 2: heartbeats run every `heartbeat.ms` on every cluster, busy or idle (README). Step 3: so an idle resource sends frames of its own, which SC-13 forbids; 100,000 resources would also need 100,000 ports on a member.

BUY.why: 100,000 resources would be 100,000 streams, or subjects of a few streams, on the outside log. E-44 ran four patterns on a handful, so cost, create time and drop are unshown.
BUY.closes: E-36's runs on the outside log

default.why: Learners or relays are in the row's design, and a relay with any delay keeps every subscribe property (E-31, model-checked; lag is not modelled). No sim ran 80 to 150 ms links, so false failover, the lease and TTL checks and the far-read lag bar are unshown. If the user wants writes homed in several regions, the row becomes WAN bars that no row here was built or tested for, so it stays open.
default.closes: phase 2: the simulator with 80 to 150 ms links between regions (no false failover, Q-21's lease and TTL checks, far-read lag)

ISR.why: It has no learners (V `full`), so far regions can follow only through relays, which keep the subscribe properties with any delay (E-31). No sim ran wide links; with multi-region writes it would face WAN bars nobody tested.
ISR.closes: phase 2: the simulator with 80 to 150 ms links between regions (no false failover, Q-21's lease and TTL checks, far-read lag)

PD.why: TiKV places learners in far regions and serves follower reads (cited as the row's precedent). No sim here ran 80 to 150 ms links for it; with multi-region writes it would face WAN bars nobody tested.
PD.closes: a PD-shaped kernel in the simulator with wide links; not planned

V4.why: v4 has no learner role and no rule that keeps a far member from voting; far regions could only run clients. Its scale tier has no wide-link run; with multi-region writes it would face WAN bars nobody tested.
V4.closes: v4's scale tier with 80 to 150 ms links

BUY.why: Far-region reads would use the outside log's own mirrors, which E-44 did not run. With multi-region writes it would face WAN bars nobody tested.
BUY.closes: a two-region run on the outside log

default.why: On the shared journal a 1 MiB record ten times a second raised others' p99 by 1.18 times in one set of three runs and 1.26 in another, against 1.2 (E-35): at the bar, inside the noise. The test was at the journal with no replication, not inside one group, and the 64 MB row and the `too-large` refusal were not built.
default.closes: phase 2: E-35's load inside one Raft group with replication, with more runs, and the tests for 1 MB records, 64 MB rows and `too-large`

MIN-P.why: On the shared journal the ratio was 1.18 and 1.26 times in two sets of runs, against 1.2 (E-35): at the bar. `pslot` also puts one resource's big record in the batch of a group that other resources share, which no experiment ran (K-06), and the size limits were not built.
MIN-P.closes: phase 2: E-35's load inside one Raft group with replication, with more runs, and the tests for 1 MB records, 64 MB rows and `too-large`

COMP.why: On the shared journal the ratio was 1.18 and 1.26 times in two sets of runs, against 1.2 (E-35): at the bar. `pslot` also puts one resource's big record in the batch of a group that other resources share, which no experiment ran (K-06), and the size limits were not built.
COMP.closes: phase 2: E-35's load inside one Raft group with replication, with more runs, and the tests for 1 MB records, 64 MB rows and `too-large`

ISR.why: A log file per group gave 1.16 times beside the big writer, but its victims are 1.19 times slower alone, and it loses to a journal from 256 groups (E-35, E-12). No run was inside one replicated partition, and the size limits were not built.
ISR.closes: phase 2: E-35's load inside one Raft group with replication, with more runs, and the tests for 1 MB records, 64 MB rows and `too-large`

OBJ.why: A 1 MB conditional PUT costs 7 to 11 ms at p99 on MinIO here (E-28). What it does to other partitions that share the writer's batch was not measured, and the size limits were not built.
OBJ.closes: E-35's load on the object-store commit path

PD.why: Its regions share an LSM store's write path on each server; nothing here measured a 1 MB record beside small ones on it.
PD.closes: E-35's load on a PD-shaped prototype; not planned

V4.why: v4 keeps a WAL per resource, the shape E-35's journal-per-group variant measured at 1.16 times. v4's own path was not run with 1 MB records, and E-43 found that one 41-byte record can make a 10 MB row with nothing refusing it.
V4.closes: E-35's load on v4's own write path, and a size-limit test

BUY.why: JetStream takes records up to about 1 MB by default (cited in SC-15's own source). Its neighbours' p99 beside a big writer and the 64 MB row in frames were not run.
BUY.closes: E-35's load on the outside log
